subject.title: fix(kimi): use k3 as single API model id, drop k3[1m] wire-id (#111561)

question: Is the current split live test sufficient for merging a change that alters K3’s compatibility alias and advertised context capacity, or should the PR show one real OpenClaw resolver-to-Kimi request starting with `kimi/k3[1m]`?
rationale: The patch uses the correct provider-owned hooks, but the provided authenticated transcript proves a direct `k3` request rather than the complete legacy-selection path users rely on.

options.title: Require end-to-end legacy-ID proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted real OpenClaw run beginning with `kimi/k3[1m]` that shows the outgoing request uses `k3`; this is the recommended merge gate.

options.title: Accept the split proof
options.body: Accept the direct normalizer assertion plus authenticated `k3` request as sufficient evidence for the compatibility rewrite.

recommendation.title: Require end-to-end legacy-ID proof
recommendation.body: Ask for a redacted real OpenClaw run beginning with `kimi/k3[1m]` that shows the outgoing request uses `k3`; this is the recommended merge gate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns Kimi provider normalization and is best placed to judge whether the hook-level proof covers the intended runtime contract.
